one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event sits in the window: the Q3 2026 print on Tue 2026-11-10 before the open (guide sales $36-37M, non-GAAP GM 46.5-47.5%, EPS -0.20 to -0.12 [5]; Street revenue 36.6 [12]). The company has beaten the top of its revenue guide 4/4 (median +8.4% vs the midpoint [2-5]), so a beat is expected and largely priced; what moves the stock is the Q4 guide. Industry read-across is mixed: Nordic's Q3 was +32% with a Q4 guide of $215-235M (flat-to-down q/q) [17], ST's MCU demand is above supply with distribution inventory below target [40] (good for demand, bad for Ambiq's wafer/OSAT allocation: OSATs ~90% utilised, substrate constrained [23,22]), and Garmin's fitness growth slowed to +16% with memory-cost price rises coming [20]. The Q3 call already flagged supply limits, so a Q4 guide at or modestly above Street (39.6 [12]) is my central case. I centre the ladder at 43.6 (+0.7%, the small post-beat drift) with a 25% monthly sigma (82% annual / 3.5 = 23%, lifted for the print), close to symmetric.

downside.story: P10: a top-3 wearable customer (78% of Q2 net sales [6]) moves a program to Nordic/ST/in-house, the wearable unit market keeps shrinking (IDC -4.3% [19]) as memory-cost price rises hit 2027 devices (Garmin [20]), OSAT/substrate cost hikes are not passed on (-2 pt GM), and the MCU upcycle (ST demand above supply [40]) rolls over, compressing EV/NTM sales by 2.5x to ~2.5x (STM-like).

base.story: Thread driver set with US FY27 growth +20% (not +25%) and FY27 opex 101 (not 105.5): FY26 revenue 138.5 (+91%), FY27 173.0 (+25%), FY28 207.6 (+20%); GM 47.3% -> 48.8%; still loss-making on non-GAAP operating income through FY29; the stock holds ~5x EV/NTM sales, the peer median.

upside.story: P90: supply eases, smart rings (Oura +74% [21]) and AI glasses (+263% [39]) add sockets, Apollo510 Lite/Atomiq non-wearable wins convert (>25% of next year's funnel [24]), GM +1.5 pt, and the stock re-rates toward edge-AI growth peers (LSCC 12.5x) to ~8.8x EV/NTM sales.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: None taken beyond the k-rule. reasoning: Started from the thread's quarterly driver set (end-customer HQ geography revenue, non-GAAP GM, non-GAAP opex) and tested its drivers against the rest of the value chain. Demand: Nordic, the closest listed peer, grew 32% in Q3 2026 with consumer +25% [17,18]; Oura's S-1 shows +74% revenue [21] and AI glasses grew 263% in H1 [39], but the wrist-worn unit market fell 4.3% (IDC) [19] and Garmin's fitness growth decelerated to +16% with memory-driven price rises planned for 2027 [20]. So I cut FY27 US growth from +25% to +20%. Supply: MCU lead times 40-52+ weeks, OSATs ~90% utilised with 8-20% price hikes, substrate constrained [22,23], and ST reports demand above supply [40]; peers are passing cost through (Lattice +30%, TI +10-15%), so I keep the GM path but take -2 pt in the downside. Opex: FY26 ~85 includes $7-10M IP purchases [24], so FY27 opex 101 (+17%) instead of 105.5. Valuation: losses rule out earnings multiples, so EV/NTM sales on a 9-peer set (5 good, 4 incumbents, both medians 4.96x) with the k=0.8 shrink; AMBQ already sits at the median, so exit = 4.99x. A Nordic EV/gross-profit leg (0.2) corrects for the GM gap. Moratorium: thread's -7.9M taken as an adjustment (no data-center revenue; my lane found no supplier or customer tying Ambiq to data centers). Scenarios move the drivers (US -15/+12%, China -40/+10%, RoW -20/+25%, GM -2/+1.5 pt) and the multiple to STM-like ~2.5x / ~8.8x. Sources: 23 of 41 tagged in-lane (peer and supply-chain data); the rest are the company's filings and releases for basic facts (56%, short of the 60% aim, because the thread set's 16 filing/consensus sources are carried for its driver citations). Not driver-linked: the custom EV/GP leg (static per share).

model_inputs.ebit_basis_note: EBIT = company non-GAAP gross profit - non-GAAP operating expense - D&A = GAAP loss from operations + SBC + severance + IPO-related bonus and transaction costs - the 2025 non-monetary gain (Ex.99.1 reconciliations). Q2 2026: -8.727 + 3.557 = -5.170 = 15.989 - 19.374 - 1.785 [5]. The company's own non-GAAP figures exclude D&A as well as SBC, so its "non-GAAP operating loss" (GP - opex) is EBITDA-like; this set deducts D&A to keep EBIT an EBIT (engine ebitda = ebit + da = the company figure). EPS in notes = company non-GAAP net loss per share (excl. SBC and D&A, incl. other income) on weighted basic shares, the basis of the guide and Street (StockAnalysis/Benzinga). Engine model EPS = EBIT / diluted shares (no other income) and is lower; Zacks figures are on a different, GAAP-like basis.

quarters.note: FY = calendar year. Actual = FY2025 (10-K [8]) + Q1 2026 (10-Q, release [4]) + Q2 2026 (10-Q [6], release [5]). model_inputs.structure_note: Thread quarterly driver set (us_rev, cn_rev, row_rev, ng_gm, ng_opex; 100% of revenue driven) with agent_2 changes to us_rev (FY27+ x0.96) and ng_opex (FY27+ x0.9573). So the value is carried by EV / NTM sales at the horizon (weight 0.8) on the 9-peer median with the k = 0.8 shrink, plus a Nordic-anchored EV / NTM gross-profit custom leg (weight 0.2) that corrects for AMBQ's lower gross margin; the moratorium expected value is an adjustment.
